logline: An Anglo-Indian Kolkata detective investigates the murder of a teenager from a powerful family while battling her own demons, in a noir thriller adapted from the novel City of Death.

renewal.note: Seven-episode limited series adapted from a standalone novel. No Season 2 announced.

bollymeter.basis: Atmospheric Kolkata noir elevated by a committed Karisma Kapoor, undercut by a sluggish pace and a predictable murder-mystery that delivers no surprises in seven episodes.

pull_quotes.text: Karisma Kapoor is very watchable, but her Rita Brown is too much of a literary formula to make a dent.
Brown tries to balance atmospheric depth with a sluggish plot, and the balance does not always hold.

seasons.review_body: Brown arrived carrying the weight of a major Karisma Kapoor comeback and the atmospheric promise of Kolkata noir. Critics landed in a familiar split: the performance camp found her uninhibited and physically committed, genuinely shedding the glitzy legacy. The craft camp noted that director Abhinay Deo builds a richly textured world, only to let it sink under a standard premise and a pacing that tests patience across seven episodes. The murder mystery offers no real surprises, and reviewers across outlets flagged cliches and formula. What rescues it from a skip is the texture of the setting and the lead performance. The reception settled as mixed-to-slightly-positive, with most critics recommending it as a one-time watch for Kapoor fans rather than a standout thriller on its own terms.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Detective Rita Brown is called to investigate the death of a teenager connected to one of Kolkata's most powerful families. The ZEE5 noir establishes its period-adjacent atmosphere efficiently; Karisma Kapoor's physicality signals immediately this is a different kind of role for her.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Rita Brown's first crime scene walk-through - all body language, no exposition.

critic_note.text: Karisma Kapoor is very watchable, but her Rita Brown is too much of a literary formula to make a dent.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 3
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The powerful family's internal fractures start showing as Rita digs deeper. The Kolkata production design earns its keep in this episode - every location choice feels specific to a city rather than a generic streaming backdrop.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Rita confronting the family patriarch - the scene where the atmosphere finally matches the stakes.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 5
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Mid-season, the investigation turns toward a suspect who complicates Rita's assumptions. The pacing problem the series has been accumulating starts to show; what worked in the noir setup now strains across the longer running time.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A late-night confrontation on the Kolkata riverbank - atmospheric, if a little too on-the-nose.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 7
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the central murder with a twist that critics found functional rather than surprising. Kapoor carries the conclusion on performance alone; the screenplay delivers the required answers without delivering genuine shock.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Brown's closing monologue - Kapoor at her most committed in a season that asked a lot of her.
